page.layout: One page of running text, no margin notes. Heading "SECT. 4." with its title "De literis quiescentibus:" at the top. Then the body in paragraphs, followed by the page number at the top, and the signature "D 4." and catchword "Sect. 5." at the foot.

main_text.head: SECT. 4.
main_text.p: Literæ אהוי[?] interdum quiescunt; id est non pronunciantur, quia vocalibus destitutæ (vulgo Ehevi vel Jehu memoriæ causa dicuntur). Hoc accidit literis אהו in medio & fine vocis, literæ ה in fine tantum.
א quiescit post vocalem longam, aliquando post Pathach & Segol:
י[?] quiescit, initio in Schurec sequente Sche-va, aut unâ ex literis בגדכפת[?]. In medio in Schurec & Cholem, & similiter in fine.
י[?] quiescit in medio & fine in Chirec, sæpe in Tsere & Segol.
ה in fine tantum quiescit, idque in Camets, Tsere, Cholem, & Segol

Apud Chaldæos, א quiescit in Camets, Tseri, & Patach, ut לא non, ראש caput. בלשצר Belschazar. ו in Chirec & Tsere, ut מלכי Rex meus. מלכי Reges. ה In Camets & Tsere, ut גלה revelabit, גלה revelat, utrumque tamen rarius, quia ה finale Hebræorum plerunque hic mutatur in Aleph, nisi aliud Aleph præcedat.
De his quatuor literis verum etiam est (quod supra de literis ejusdem organi dictum) quod facile inter se permutentur.

page.notes: The Hebrew letters and vowel points in the first paragraph (אהוי) and the small leading marks before "quiescit" (read as י[?]) are doubtful. The word in the third paragraph (בגדכפת) is doubtful. Hebrew forms in the Chaldean paragraph (לא, ראש, בלשצר, מלכי, גלה) are read as printed but their vowel points are not fully legible. The printed "Tfere", "Tferi", "Tfe:e" are read as Tsere, Tseri; the long s is plain s throughout. The "ct" in "dictum" is a ligature read as ct. Page number "(7)" and signature "D 4." are as printed at the head and foot.
